title: Central banks tighten again as oil, chips and politics pull markets apart
dek: The ECB raised rates, the Fed argued about whether to follow, Korean chip stocks slumped and Brent jumped above $105 — yet Wall Street still finished the week higher.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.explanation: The VIX — the options market's gauge of expected swings in the S&P 500 — closed at 15.47 on Monday, down about 9.5% over the month, and US indices set a record week, yet CNN's Fear & Greed index sits at 45, in "fear", and high-yield credit spreads edged up to 3.15 points on 8 October. Reddit chatter is split between broad index funds and memory-chip names, which is a sign of attention chasing the AI trade rather than broad conviction.

regions.headline: Record week for stocks, but rates and rents still bite
regions.summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,811.54 on 9 October, up 1.15% on the week, while the Russell 2000 of smaller firms fell 0.91%. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.22% on 8 October and the average 30-year mortgage rate was 7.40%, keeping borrowing costs high for households and small businesses. A partial government shutdown over Homeland Security funding rumbled on, and the president set up a committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook.

regions.headline: ECB lifts rates to 2.5% as French unrest tests bond market
regions.summary: The European Central Bank raised its deposit rate to 2.5% on Friday, blaming energy costs, and a Reuters poll of economists expects another rise in December with inflation near double the 2% target. Euro area HICP inflation was 3.23% in August. France faced its most violent school protests in decades while its prime minister promised energy price curbs and a release of diesel stocks.

regions.headline: Korean chip selloff deepens as Tokyo and Hong Kong hold up
regions.summary: The KOSPI fell 8.42% over the week as foreign investors sold chip shares. The Nikkei 225 rose 1.06% and is up 8.72% in a month, with the yen at 158.61 per dollar and the Bank of Japan reporting broadening inflation pressure. China's Shanghai Composite slipped 0.69% ahead of trade figures, and the World Bank lifted its view on India's growth.

watchNextWeek: US September CPI and retail sales (Investopedia preview of the week ahead)
Big US bank results, which open the third-quarter earnings season
IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, with debt and the Middle East on the agenda
Further US congressional talks on Homeland Security funding and the partial shutdown
body:
## The week in one paragraph

Two central banks moved in the opposite direction to the one most people assumed a year ago: the European Central Bank [raised its deposit rate to 2.5%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNV0tWM0xZcmxXSUZReDVWQ0NycWY2ZW5ZaVFEdjh0SmtWWHRCMjVLdTVvV1dKRTNZX1FTeEZxNUxtQjR1LWJmeE5kLUFiT2NWZ1hBU0tEWXVXNHMwX3NUZnZHbUU5aUNMcExtejVEejhEOURxb2ZVa2daVnFZZ0dWclZXZ0ZOb3RJX2trQk9PcFIwSzdIcHpEY01GNzVwSjdQdGZTbTNDR3FEQQ?oc=5) on Friday, and a senior US Federal Reserve official spent the week [playing down the chance of a rate *rise* this month](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxNckNMd0xCc1RMemJpSlNXQVBEeVFKUktQWmFwTlBZWTFrM19DWTA1d1dtN3djS0tSbTY3VzhWYlp2NEdpQ1RIdUthT2xGMVhPNmxqRXFyUEloVVNRQWZ6S3VQeHlZaklEbGh2SWRmckNONnZXaV81TjItOTAwZlBPakZsTzRoVHpMUDVEYlFpbTJraXM?oc=5). Energy is the reason. Brent crude closed at $105.60 on Monday, up 5.26% on the week, after [record tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxNOURnWGRjbThEV2lBS0EyTWpZQVdDNER1MnVvSFJDR3ZjaFR3Rl9QVkZPc1RnT1lKRnZwU0hDRnlMLXZQM3l6VlI5M1YzdXFvM2pqNldLc2ZpVkV5UThEV0RHVkZTUkZVTE9WV215UEY4U01ZbVlVN2ZwOEJjQ3hiZ1pZanhodVduZTVWbA?oc=5) and [production shut in ahead of a hurricane](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxONW0wejJNQmpGTE9heFBmZG8wTWE5a010VFNMSDBqcThNXzBFTjZkbWF3NnpxSWxoVkRJSEhMcDk4VDh5OVp3bzlZNzdiS0pNTnd6aGkwQVZsU0JiOU9wb0k1ckN1V2ZUVl9sTFRuZnVhLXFlaDUwZGIxT2VxNW1RZUwyNlJ3c2ZxRkdONll5RVdtTnlfcDllN0pnLWE4VU1FblRvbHdkTkIwbHNk?oc=5), before easing as Washington [touted an "energy ceasefire"](https://news.google.?oc=5). Against that, the S&P 500 still had [a record-breaking week](https://news.google.?oc=5), closing at 7,811.54 on 9 October, up 1.15%. South Korea's market was the outlier, down 8.42%.

## United States

The headline numbers look calm; the plumbing does not. The 10-year Treasury yield — the benchmark that drags mortgage and corporate borrowing costs with it — was 5.22% on 8 October, with the two-year at 4.75%. The gap between them (the "yield curve") was 0.44 points on 9 October, a normal upward slope rather than the recession-signalling inversion of recent years.

For households the squeeze is concrete: the average 30-year mortgage rate was 7.40% on 8 October, up from 7.28% a week earlier, and commentators are now [asking whether 8% is next](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMizAFBVV95cUxPdFNPbDNtTWJfTzlPMkhtSkJqVVVvOFJ0TmhQakVFbWxyY3p4NDU3T3h2bG40cVl3V1dxTGFWRm1WUnVRY01MZ21HRExFYTRzRE8tVkFqbmg2UTJUdmF2VzU0a0s1aTZ2emZXZTRxRVpka2VwcGV4LTBFdVZDbUpnRjV2MmxybmFMQm1FUG03dXNkVFdKeGxPNnM2V2RTdE90bS14M1NqOU52UlB4QVp4c3NvQmNiM0djeDg4Y19Jd2tLYW5hU3FqWHJmUFE?oc=5). Inflation was 3.71% in August, up from 3.54% in July, though core inflation (stripping out food and energy) was softer at 2.76%. The New York Fed published research arguing that [price rises on many everyday items were entirely down to tariffs](https://news.google.?oc=5) — a reminder for finance directors that import duties show up in customer prices with a lag.

Unemployment was 4.2% in September, a touch above August's 4.1%. Smaller companies, more exposed to domestic borrowing costs, lagged: the Russell 2000 fell 0.91% on the week while the Nasdaq added 0.64%.

Politics intruded on the Fed itself. The president [established a committee to investigate governor Lisa Cook](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijwFBVV95cUxQLWhUWUhLVjBvQUV1WWxNZ1lHZUxWbWpoQW9jckFpa284cmRTMkloVmdYaE1nR19sc2F0NFdWenEzWWlfRTd2elQzdTczcnFYTTJMTW9hQTY3eUxyR0xqcjB6cE9CSlloUGtFcXVzVzZTUl82RFZneGFvWDcwWHRNMEtETXYySTEtVlhYUDVrbw?oc=5), the latest attempt to remove her, after the [Supreme Court blocked the firing for now](https://news.google.?oc=5). Investors generally dislike uncertainty about who sets rates; so far it has not shown up in the bond market.

## Euro area

The ECB's move to 2.5% was explicitly about [energy costs feeding through](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNV0tWM0xZcmxXSUZReDVWQ0NycWY2ZW5ZaVFEdjh0SmtWWHRCMjVLdTVvV1dKRTNZX1FTeEZxNUxtQjR1LWJmeE5kLUFiT2NWZ1hBU0tEWXVXNHMwX3NUZnZHbUU5aUNMcExtejVEejhEOURxb2ZVa2daVnFZZ0dWclZXZ0ZOb3RJX2trQk9PcFIwSzdIcHpEY01GNzVwSjdQdGZTbTNDR3FEQQ?oc=5). Euro area inflation was 3.23% in August, up from 2.93% in July, and a [Reuters poll now points to another hike in December](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxPNVlkaVBmN0lBelRFMEktcDh1aG5GZElENVRtWngwa1VzQ0pRaFU5bU9mQnE0ZDVna3JFRVV3ZW1qZHgxYlNvRUJLWmV4WnVxbWhwWVRKLVdfVzBNbFhLSlU4NmhSMmxSQi1hYTF4U1ZJQ3dGNjRNUklHMHY5ZjJEamZ4ZXVkT3J0X3VaVGNQSkJzNWtVNVZuTlVURFZWYnRJdmdtS3hpQ0kzVl9W?oc=5) with inflation close to double the 2% target. One governing council member said [risks were to the upside and more tightening might be needed](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOUUg5SHpBLWFwbG5xWEVMN2lFV1ZkS3VqN3dXTHQxM2RLcVk5QmtrMzFjNTk4S214czN4X2NyZjVULV8yazNYSC1qeERUNFA0N0dmajVjT3FXVUpFcW1aMjNickdUakg1dkdKSTZXZG5NRXdzY2M1SWp3QnBjejJVWFdRekZTZ0hwMWJ0cDZrU2ZhRXliV0lSck9SbmgwZmswWGhSRmJfX2JsMzRkNG5sbQ?oc=5). For euro-area businesses that means loan pricing drifting up again just as the economy was recovering: euro area GDP grew 1.16% in the year to the second quarter, better than 0.54% in the first. Unemployment held at 6.4% in August.

France is the stress point. The country saw [its most violent school protests in decades](https://news.google.?oc=5), with [classes suspended](https://news.google.?oc=5), while the prime minister promised [energy price curbs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxOdnhCVzNzNW45NVJNYldmRVN4R3Y5c2JyYmhmVEI2NUJOTkRSWTRZV3BjNUtBSnI4TXhjRXQ4c0NFSHZHVk8wYkdIWWl0aGtQcm1QVlF6NnhYaU1vWjRPYjY1OHl3cFYwZjY5VHlZUXJoZ0I5YWpkWlRTdTJLRzZJX2l1RjNTYm1LQ2x3YlFoa3RDUHl4QmNKZTkxQnp2QkVMTjZjMlB2UlJ6Tm1JTG9UMUdnTQ?oc=5) and the [release of 10 million barrels of diesel from state stocks](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxOaWFYZU9aMFBWYnZnMWVubE5TTlVVUW5sa2JSbkpQM2dnbTctV3VUeGtVTG9rVE8yR0E0aW5pWlYwR0JMRTEtWDFqTzIxZVFLbS1tZFhPTjlLQ0V5UFZqX2Roa1puV1lTUHpXSnJUODcxRURHUEFEVWMwakFWcVJ2bHZTR1N0X0NBN0Q1WXdRLUdFZUtrenVEcGlBbFNkWG5ZYUVtTUU4M3V1aS1CaE9F?oc=5). Analysts framed the country as [caught between angry students and unforgiving bond markets](https://news.google.?oc=5); the Bank of France governor insisted [France does not need ECB help at present](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxNOGxLaHh3Yk11empidnZOcmNpN2Z0NFoxazNON2xDb0xnakhYejhZSVVubE5oOXlFXy1sUXp0ODd2aFlZTmphZFlqX1RhR3FLazFkd0FkMzM0Y1FwTWdVSHNQSzU0bWhnQ240dGhKRHdFU3dNOXpVZEw5eUVQR2FqRk5xa0c0OFhFazNFQXM2aFR4N3dwb2JzMnh5dUF6MlBYUEk4TGQ0U2hQYUNYUDBXUmdB?oc=5). The CAC 40 is down 3.75% over a month, the weakest of the big European indices.

Elsewhere, the EU adopted [nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings targeting Russia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQNHU4aWdseGJQNDlHSkY2bVlVakhtNG9qSWo2eHl0MV9WSTRoc1lqdUdTcHlXeWdCVU1nZ3V6c2Z2dV9FMmRXdGlmMjhOOVpENE9ZRkY1UkRxM1ZzUTBaLTE0OUhEUE9nVzFVd1pUQUlJcjljeWhjNEJvSk55VlhobmU5Q0F2S2lKb0M0Z2lLcjg1Y1J2bG8zUU8xUXdLUV93WUpOMG5DSE11dzJmdklv?oc=5) and reached a deal with Beijing to ["moderate" Chinese car exports into the bloc](https://news.google.?oc=5) — relevant to anyone importing vehicles or components. In the UK, the FTSE 100 rose 1.08% on the week while a think tank warned the chancellor faces [a £35bn Budget challenge](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE5JbGp6RWhnc2h1eEJoLUdMbDVVZk5IRkNvdXpUSUlHdHNOd0JLT1RoODJHTmVNZV85cUhkRVR3bEV2SkoxUkZqUm44SE9xUE50WXhpSEtmN3BRUEk?oc=5).

## Asia

Korea stole the week for the wrong reasons. The KOSPI fell 8.42% as [a chip selloff deepened and foreign selling persisted](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE9id1k0b0ZFY0JFbzEtNXloQ2JCeGZzbEZzQng3ekFsU2lfNUFxWnpjcXVWT2hadm9PQkk3ZkJ2aTc2SlVyTWpnOHpfdW1vMU1fR3RSSjhWWFhTQU1hYUFNVHhGbEduNHdYQ1U3MXhWWllKSmZUc0lOOGN3?oc=5), with reports that [overseas investors are stepping back from the AI trade](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxPSVM0eGxqTmhzVlVmY2dtV21BMkFTQ0h4eU5tMUNGdXgtSzEyMlpvZWRFT05teDVlZG9sMC1HREI1d282VkI4UEdtUU0wUlFLY0ZkOGZlSEIzbFJsRlVEQzBSVW5TdFo2NUtuenUySXdmdzN4RmpwaExQM0JvalEtaEdQWmFrNGxFRHV0b093R2RPWXA1NnZmMUt3SmRmSFp6Ql9zMDRvdC1rbXhPSWs4RFhnR2R2SGVwRWJMNzB5bw?oc=5) and that [domestic retail investors are switching to US markets](https://news.google.?oc=5). It is a useful warning that concentrated, single-theme markets can reverse fast.

Japan went the other way: the Nikkei closed at 69,030.92 on 9 October, up 1.06% on the week and 8.72% in a month. The yen was at 158.61 per dollar, a weak level that flatters exporters and raises import bills. The Bank of Japan [said inflationary pressure is broadening](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxQUXI2b2hNU0J1U3U3UU9ra0tmWlB4aFdsbkR4QmIxeFFKM042dDR2RUhDeFRpYnRhbWNOYVF3eE9PQmlvaTg2bGg2UjktYWE3NzhqLVhlamZmNzFhQS15SEtqVEJTZzViLXZKTkh0UEdoMTYxbUExSGE2eG1JWlJ3eTc1TjNiWGFpcFpic19PNWtzWlB0TnV6TVFJeC1YbVFvX05ZX29R?oc=5), and Japan's 10-year yield was 2.94% in August. Separately Tokyo [declared a cybersecurity emergency](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxPOU1XdTZTQzhSRXJVZzFheVNVVUw1c19RQW1Uc2Ixa29zaDF2RHdtRHVNUXdvdWEwZzBtV1p3T0p3T2g5R3F2elA1ZFlvYTJmV2lvcjhWR2VIcTZoVEY4N2RiN0pSNWp2T2RFTTRSMWRlRXkxakYtNVJ0ZzJRSERUTVgxdUhWZ3ZIZExN?oc=5) after [a spate of attacks](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijgFBVV95cUxQNkZsdWpacDdZczlUd3paV084UnlpSmJvdC02dFdwYjdGTjhMdmg3MjJiVVJES0dWdk1ka2dadWExaFEtcTB3UVZUWElfMTk3THpQdS1aUFU0VTU4aGR4SWRLdkpKVUg5YTJWUXItY1pVVjBtelZIX1hqWXkwRkh4VFBmOWdWN0hMYlpxWmFB?oc=5).

China's Shanghai Composite slipped 0.69% ahead of [trade figures that dominate Asia's data week](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxNSkVVdzRaMnhidk5OSkJHV1djRnladE1EZk5uTkRWZEIyVmJyb2JLRmREUmFHMnBPSTVxMmwweS05LVpSVHcxVWpHNXpWUkxWbTZWd01BUFBNaWs3bHpNQ2MxaVBZaDdiaVdKLXB6a3Riam80NDQ4dk45WE5qZzlQNlZhNi0?oc=5); Beijing also [agreed to import US coal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxQaDIwUmVYeElGQ1pubVptN01UOUw0YjRZUWNSSzNCbE5Nc0FVYVdYNDVtZi1uWkF1eHlJYWgtMURQNDFGaGRhdDZOSEpQUnBPVU0ydVU5dDl1Sk1LVjFqaWFjRDhiRXdUVmlxZlBPSmQ5a0pCVDM4MjA5QmZuRFlHam4tNWZIV3VKTHIxZVl4MG5oXzZZelVKZ1hOWEpNX2Et?oc=5). In India the Sensex fell 0.63%; the World Bank [lifted its growth view while warning Asia's buffers are too thin to keep absorbing an oil shock](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNblFzWXpLUGRyNWdRbzQybnZpN1N6LTVqQnRKSjRYY2xZRTdKNVQ4TG5POGlXXzZXUlU1TF9GQUJhdTBITzZoOFFXMVE1THlMekRRVm9DcEdacW9iZjM2M2JPbWpJM3M5NmQtYS15MENkZWJtR0tqdGhvZUxKNE5nNA?oc=5), and a government adviser said India is [set to overtake Japan as the fourth-biggest economy next year](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxQODVYOWZMOGYxMlZlWUVvXzJoT09TQWo3Q1dPMUFha1hOZ1RhczhhQWxrM2tFUGRyV050bmdwd25aTFlER21tdXRTc1Y3VW9LbnZyOFJ6ZzdOb3dmaWQzdUdKYTIyb2otbzRHb0dqMG9FOEduYkNJeHlTZXlKYVoxWkZmNTJOWFFWdGFzTEhuNFBlVTZK?oc=5).

## Debt and politics

Debt is back at the centre of the conversation: [Middle East war and high debt levels are set to dominate the IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxQWlZqTVZkYlUxR2xKODRtSHFhLUI5ZVk4MWlwUURPZTRJSy1UYjdKak1ZbzdGMG80dmNOTVlVbUtvbW1zUU9hWE5QeU9xc19wWE50TnR4M05sQ0c0aFI0ZmYtTGN6Q0hwanJUajNzSlRfaVBQNXdPMUlfQlpfb1JHTGlQWkg5aVdOTE5SZ29NRXZLSW85enZHa2dCOVFSWmFpUEptcWMxa1JxVW15ZGhLLTRRcDEyeXBEWkw0RnJR?oc=5). US federal debt was 122.59% of GDP in the first quarter; euro area government debt was 88.9% of GDP over the same period, up from 87.7%. In Washington a partial shutdown ground on — the House [passed a Homeland Security funding bill that the top Senate Democrat called "dead on arrival"](https://news.google.?oc=5), Democrats [sent a counteroffer to the White House](https://news.google.?oc=5) and the president said he would [sign an order directing DHS to pay TSA workers](https://news.google.?oc=5). Geopolitics stayed noisy, with [Houthi attacks keeping a Saudi airport closed](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNUjJxRmNFWVFOVlEtUl9td2J5VXowU3BKQTJJd28ybW9EZ1VaRmlLZTgtbFNLTEVldC1RQTE0NDIwMU4teThZUmF1WkpsSDNwcjh1WG5vYWQxNGtMQmdydUpPSFdYeHpUb1pXVEFBRTQweFdxbkpEZlBQb2Vza2EwXw?oc=5) and [North Korea firing multiple ballistic missiles](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxPZ2FsdGE3YUJ5V3VpbjBDWEpDaF9FMk9IbE9ZWFRUZ0l2SEJmQi1pbFZxNzFscG5LVDJiUUxpRzZ3c2dvbzl0R3RWQmlKTTN0TDdwX1FST0IydGp5c0NwY0lpTTFOQklXZU5LZ2piMnBQRl9pcUg2M3VLTTVSU1k1NngwMkdab3BWeVFuUXh2NTBCTld2?oc=5).

## AI and technology

The AI build-out is increasingly a credit story. The Wall Street Journal reported that [Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX are seeking large debt deals to pay for AI chips](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxOQlQwOUh0Wlhtb1B1T1YxN1ItVmh1ck5xeE5Xa0FWR2ZRcjlDdGZSM1hUVTltMHp1aHhVM1FCYUZKNnIweDhKWjlxUGpGeVlJTFFlNElVQnBkT2VMaERTRTBCVXFTbk1BRFRPRVpRWVA2blBxbnMwR3Q4VUZVQU9iVEFyRExCVW5aSjl3bXFOYlZERUxTY0l4QjA1RS1BVjRQS1lCOW5kSWtqY0t3?oc=5), with Broadcom [in early talks on financing for OpenAI chips](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOc0VVNVE3MUUyRkpKUTJoOS1ORkVoUGc3U25aZVNhenRxMmFhQnZfeGtSdy1NNG1PNXNMMEZJa0tianRUZUtZWXNveF9zZ25RcHBJRlFHaWF3VTJ1NXBRbEV2ajFrRzdrazlEbVJPOGlMcGZ1TEZ4M0piOG56Smx0NTRiblZNWEo1aXFUbXJzQm81Qzl4ZVNkbWtyN3FWWUtwYjJWZ0RCeFJpV0tHOHBWcjNB?oc=5) reported at more than $50bn. Amazon is [in talks to buy AI start-up Decart for around $7bn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxOSTR0SUxydGYzRDJmaGtaWkRTYkkybS1GWlRkZFFnMjVXRFlZX0hHMUtVdFdIN0ZyQk0wMk1LNFhaUml3Y3FlRUV6SWFxVk9UUFg3MTUzelJtZU8tdjVpREpVS0owdkt2aVJhMUVObjg1TlRTREtZQzBINHJTTFloWDNBQTFCVl9yOE9HNXhBazJWMElncnlIZWNPdG5IY25ObFg0SGswNks5MkF0ODM4bEVRWkhjS3ZqcXVuWlVnamU0dw?oc=5), and OpenAI and Synopsys [announced a partnership on a model for chip design](https://news.google.?oc=5). One chart doing the rounds compared [data centre spending with all other construction](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPVlM2LW9IQTdURFB4LThSMlpVWHpkMzVraE1yb3VNRDBuTkhCUWtIQmk2bk5RTTFZWjhYaGxGSnV6djZEZnRBY2xIT1F1WFdlY3JKa2pNZzVtR0xkdDZ0VldxUi04LWROamtLYWxVTzdlSVZLUjJmZ3ZOVjJzMWVMSWt1Qi14QQ?oc=5). On the policy side, Microsoft's president said [AI is less regulated than milk](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTFBWblVtb0hnbURUVU1uMXNTMmFyUmxwUGNETm1ZUmpGRVJmcVdUVVlzT2N4LUFzbVRkLVVtR1VvWURJc3NYRkhoY0Q4UDRGTm9sZWxhUVJvMThuWTQ?oc=5) and Bill Gates called [cyberattacks the most imminent AI threat](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxQQlk1MEkxSmlfblJNdU1oY1l1NlFCMWQ1VTN5RHRkQkgyclF4aV9WcGJHODdZTTJSTldVcDdtd0xfX0pHcDJyZkZxaEU4aW1hY2FFb2JpNDJFd2dRcUJVek9OUVVJWF81U1hEY09iNlQyd0l3RHdfV0JfMzFRMkNjQnhPSjFvTUJDeWVrZUFMX3JWNldJbFpqMg?oc=5).

## Company news and results

Earnings season restarts this week, with [big banks reporting first](https://news.google.?oc=5). Among results already filed with the SEC, Constellation Brands reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 net sales of $2,633m, up 6% year on year, reported operating income of $805m, down 8%, and reported earnings per share of $3.32 against comparable EPS of $3.74; it [updated its fiscal 2027 reported EPS outlook to $11.85–$12.55 and reaffirmed its comparable range of $11.20–$11.90](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16918/000001691826000039/stzex991_83120268kearnings.htm). The company also disclosed the acquisition of a spirit-based ready-to-drink brand for $75m at close plus up to $278m contingent on future performance, and declared a quarterly dividend of $1.03 per share.

Other large filers in the week included [PepsiCo](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77476/000007747626000050/pep-20261008.htm) and [Delta Air Lines](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27904/000002790426000035/dal-20261009.htm), both of which lodged quarterly results with the SEC; their exhibits were not available through our filing reader.

## Market mood

Mixed, and oddly so. The VIX closed at 15.47 on Monday, down roughly 9.5% over a month — calm by any standard — yet CNN's Fear & Greed index, which blends seven market signals on a 0–100 scale, reads 45, or "fear", barely changed from 44 a week earlier though well above last month's 33. High-yield credit spreads — the extra interest riskier companies pay over the government — were 3.15 points on 8 October, up from 3.09 the day before: a small widening, not a rupture. The dollar index rose 0.2% on the week and the euro slipped to 1.12. Gold at $4,203.60 and copper up 2.79% suggest hedging and industrial demand are both alive. On Reddit, the most-discussed tickers were a mix of broad S&P 500 and Nasdaq trackers and memory- and AI-linked chip names — unverified retail opinion, but a fair gauge of where attention sits.

## What to watch next week

US September inflation and retail sales land alongside [the opening of bank earnings season](https://news.google.?oc=5); China's trade numbers are the Asian focus; and finance ministers gather in Bangkok with debt on the agenda.

*This is commentary, not investment advice.*
